To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spinach chloroplast fragments catalyzed photochemical oxidation of 3 aromatic compounds: 1) 3,4-benzoquinone (BQ), 2) 3,5,3',4'-tetrachlorobiphenyl (TCBP) and 3) 3,3',4,4'-tetrabromobiphenyl  (TBP).
spinach chloroplast fragments can catalyse photochemical oxidation of aromatic compounds.
the photoreaction of aromatic compounds by chloroplasts is catalyzed by a flavoprotein and a cytochrome, and that the flavoprotein is a flavin mononucleotide (FMN).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photochemical reactivity of aromatic compounds in spinach chloroplasts.
the photochemical reactions of aromatic compounds with isolated chloroplasts.
the study of the photophysical properties of chlorophylls in the presence of a variety of compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photochemical activity of spinach chloroplast fragments with aromatic compounds is not due to a photosensitizing action of the aromatic compound but rather due to the formation of a photosensitizer in the chloroplast.

the  photoreaction  of  aromatic  hydrocarbons,  in  the  presence  of  spinach  chloroplast  fragments,  proceeds  by  a  mechanism  which  is  similar  to  the  photooxidation of aromatic hydrocarbons in the absence of chloroplast fragments.

the 2-phenyl-1,3-butadiene isomerization is a photochemical reaction which is  dependent on the presence of oxygen, and which is catalyzed by the enzyme  ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photochemical activity of spinach chloroplasts with benzene, naphthalene and anthracene is not due to singlet oxygen but to free radical reactions.

we are studying the photochemical activity of the chloroplast in terms of the photochemical reactions that are catalyzed by the chloroplast, the photochemical reactions of aromatic compounds, and the photochemical activity in the presence of both the chloroplast and the aromatic compound.
the photodynamic activity of chloroplast fragments with aromatic compounds can be divided into three categories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloroplast fragments are not only able to catalyze the formation of the aromatic compounds, but they are also able to catalyse the formation of the chloroplast fragments.
chloroplasts are able to carry out a wide range of reactions with aromatic compounds and that the reactions are not limited to those that are catalyzed by the enzymes in the chloroplasts.
chloroplasts from spinach leaves can be isolated and used for the photocatalytic oxidation of aromatic compounds.
